sentences.text: It is his case that the respondent - Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran laid pipeline from his agricultural land in the year 1997 which is completed in the year 2005-06.
For the first time, he made a representation on 17.12.2012 requesting to the Executive Engineer of Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran to grant compensation by starting acquisition proceeding.

3. The learned advocate Mr. Gunale for the petitioner vehemently argued that the petitioner time and again approached the authorities by making oral requests and still no proceeding is initiated under the Land Acquisition Act.
The valuable land of the petitioner is now affected because of the pipeline.
In spite of his representation, no steps are taken.
He thus prays that the directions be issued by allowing the writ petition.
4. At the outset, learned A.G.P. objects the petition on the ground of maintainability.
In his submission, the petition suffers from delay and laches as in the year 1997-1998 the pipeline was laid down and till 2012 he did not made even representation.
He submits that making oral request cannot be said to be pursuation.
There is no representation provided under the Act and even on that count the petitioner would not get any cause of action.
He prays for dismissal of the petition.
5. The learned advocate for Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran also opposes the petition on the ground of delay and laches.
6. The learned advocate for respondent No. 5 also opposes the petition.
7. It is admittedly a position that in the year 1997-1998 the work of laying down pipeline was undertaken.
The proceeding was also undertaken under the Land Acquisition Act wherever, the pipeline is laid down.

It is appearing from the affidavit in reply by the Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran that work of the scheme was completed on 31.12.1997 and the same is transferred to the Municipal Council on 21.01.1998.
Thus, the petition is filed after more than 12 years.
8. The learned advocate Mr. Gunale in the course of argument has pointed out the circulars of the Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran wherein, the proper procedure required is stated.
However, this Court finds that, the petitioner himself has 4 10-wp 6341-2014.odt approached after 15 years though it is stated that the work of the scheme is going on till 2004-2005.
There is no such material seen on record.
An affidavit of the Maharashtra Jeevan Pradhikaran is clear stating that the work is already handed over after completion of the scheme.
On these grounds, this Court cannot accept the case of the petitioner that the scheme is completed in the year 2004-2005 and that till 2012 he was making only oral requests.

For all these reasons this Court finds that, certainly, the petition suffers from delay and laches and the petition deserves to be dismissed.
9.
The writ petition stands dismissed.
No order as to costs.
10. In view of dismissal of writ petition, pending civil application also stands disposed of.
